subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmark criteria, latency/cost, model shortlist) - ACME
messages:
From: Dave Li <dave.li@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - ACME / Redwood follow-up

Thanks again for the demo today - appreciated the clear answers on routing and cost controls. As discussed on the call, our engineering and procurement teams want a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the technical evaluation milestone so we can align internal stakeholders. Key asks from our side:

- Benchmark success criteria (latency targets P95, throughput, quality thresholds for classification/generation)
- Cost targets or expected $/1k tokens for the evaluation workload
- Shortlist of model variants we should evaluate (open models + Redwood-recommended variants)
- Runtime / infra requirements (GPU type, memory, expected run duration)

We'd like a draft MAP we can circulate by end of next week to keep our internal approval timeline (procurement wants a plan by 12/01). Target close for this eval milestone is ~2026-12-15. Can you send a draft with milestones, owners, and dependencies?

Attaching our evaluation spec (acme-eval-specs.pdf) and the call notes. Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if that helps.
—Dave
Dave Li
Head of ML Engineering, ACME AI
dave.li@acme.ai

Attachment: acme-eval-specs.pdf (spec outline, dataset details)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dave Li <dave.li@acme.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - ACME / Redwood follow-up

Hi Dave - thanks for the clear notes and for sharing the eval spec. Per our call, attached is a draft MAP focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone plus a Redwood benchmark template you can use to capture results. High-level summary below; the full MAP is attached (MAP_v1_ACME.pdf).

Draft MAP (Technical Evaluation milestone) - target close 2026-12-15
- Milestone: Baseline benchmark run & quality validation (owner: ACME engineering) - target complete 2026-11-30
  - Deliverables: filled benchmark template, example prompts, labeled QA set
  - Dependencies: ACME to provide eval slices and test harness (see acme-eval-specs.pdf)

- Milestone: Redwood benchmark runs & latency/cost profiling (owner: Redwood - Jonas) - target complete 2026-12-07
  - Deliverables: P95 latency table, tokens/sec throughput, expected $/1k tokens for each model variant, GPU instance type used
  - Dependencies: access to ACME eval set, agreed model shortlist, test harness (we can run on Dedicated or Hosted sandbox)

- Milestone: Quality review & model shortlist finalization (owner: ACME + Redwood) - target complete 2026-12-10
  - Deliverables: chosen model variant, quantization recommendation, final performance tradeoffs

- Milestone: Recommendation & next steps (owner: Marissa / ACME stakeholders) - target complete 2026-12-15
  - Deliverables: go/no-go decision, estimated monthly cost for production traffic, proposed rollout plan

Model shortlist (initial suggestion)
- Open-research candidates: Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0, mosaicml/mpt-7b-instruct (as comparators)
- Redwood-recommended variants: quantized 13B float16, int8 Q4_0 13B (low-latency), and a 7B streaming-optimized variant for low-cost low-latency checks

Benchmark success criteria (examples - open to ACME adjustment)
- Latency: P95 < 200ms for 128-token generation on dedicated infra (primary); P95 < 350ms on cost-optimized configs
- Throughput: sustain 10 req/s with batch/streaming behavior for peak scenario
- Quality: >= 92% intent extraction F1 on labeled slices; generation ROUGE / human pass rate thresholds to be defined in benchmark template
- Cost: target <$0.02 per 1k tokens for shortlisted production-like config (we'll provide measured estimates per run)

Next steps
1) Camila / Jonas - can you confirm infra recommendation (GPU family + sample run config) and whether we should run on Dedicated sandbox or Hosted?
2) Dave - if the above looks reasonable, can you share the first eval slice and a HubSpot approval note so procurement has the MAP to review?

I'm attaching the MAP draft and our benchmark template. Happy to iterate; we can also do a 30-minute technical sync this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: MAP_v1_ACME.pdf, redwood-benchmark-template.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - infra & shortlist input

Thanks Marissa - quick internal note from infra/product side:

- Recommended infra for reliable P95 <200ms for 13B variants: NVIDIA H100 or A100 80GB on Dedicated (pinned instance) for benchmark runs. For cost experiments we can run on A10G / T4 for the 7B variants.
- Suggested run configs:
  - 13B quantized int8 (Q4_0) - batch size 1 with KV cache warm-up, measure cold-start vs warmed runs
  - 13B fp16 baseline - for throughput comparison
  - 7B streaming-optimized - to evaluate low-cost low-latency baseline

- We'll need ACME to confirm whether eval traffic requires session affinity / persistent KV lifetime (some of their tests may use long contexts). That affects memory footprint and whether we recommend sharded KV cache.

Jonas - can you allocate ~8 GPU-hours on Dedicated sandbox next week (ETA 11/30) and take ownership of the Redwood benchmark runs? If yes I'll flag to infra to reserve A100/H100 windows.

Camila
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
